nativeValidation.setup: Use non-elevated PowerShell at the worker commit in a writable local NTFS checkout. Run command 1 from the checkout root, copy files.copyFrom to files.copyTo, then run commands 2 and 3 in the same checkout.
commands: if ((Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -LiteralPath '.t3-tmp/native-copy-cancel/validate-copy-cancellation.ps1').Hash.ToLowerInvariant() -ne '03a742105b7dbf07155aa5da372d10d1ee2da726c229702cb29529d4f03a4751') { throw 'Unexpected native validation script checksum.' }
expectedResults: The script runs go test '-v' '-count=10' '-timeout=2m' '-run' '^TestCopyFileEndsWithItsContext$' ./cmds/ownsand-agent/internal/vmruntime/hcsrt. All 10 repetitions pass the live, already_canceled and in_flight subtests without a skip.

The positive log contains 10 strictly partial reports from CopyFileExW at 0 < transferred < total, with a live context, pbCancel set by the watcher, a context.Canceled result and an absent destination.

The script creates a test-only overlay that cancels before the copy and verifies that the destination is absent. It runs go test '-v' '-count=1' '-timeout=2m' "-overlay=$overlayPath" '-run' '^TestCopyFileEndsWithItsContext$/^in_flight$' ./cmds/ownsand-agent/internal/vmruntime/hcsrt. This control must exit 1 with the progress assertion showing 0 of 0 and context canceled. The validation script itself succeeds.
After authorized PR publication, verify that the automatically triggered Go on Windows job passes. The job runs this package with the rest of the Go module.
nativeValidation.privilegeNotes: The native fixture uses ordinary files. It needs no symlinks, service control, state-directory ACL setup, guest image, or Hyper-V.
